verifications.claim: The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule, when fully stacked, stand 322 feet tall.' R3: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket stands ... 98m (322ft)'. R4: 'Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1 rocket ... 322 feet (98 metres) tall'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact height of the SLS rocket as 322 feet (98m).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is the most powerful rocket in operation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8.8 million pounds: Thrust at liftoff — the most powerful operational rocket' and 'It's the most powerful rocket NASA has ever launched.'
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly calls it the most powerful operational rocket.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket produces 8.8 million pounds of thrust at launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8.8 million pounds: Thrust at liftoff'. R3: 'the rocket will produce 8.8 million pounds of thrust'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly confirm the exact thrust figure for SLS at liftoff/launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is designed to carry four astronauts in the Orion capsule around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '4 astronauts' on mission to 'loop around the moon'. R3: 'crew of four astronauts ... on a 10-day journey around the Moon' aboard Orion.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS launches 4 astronauts in Orion for lunar orbit mission.

verifications.claim: The orange core stage of the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is 212 feet (65 meters) tall.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions the height of the core stage.

verifications.claim: The two white solid rocket boosters of the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket stand 177 feet (54 meters) tall.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions the height of the solid rocket boosters.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is 11 feet high.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the exact height of the Orion capsule.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is 16.5 feet wide.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule is ... 16 1/2 feet wide'. R5: 'The spacecraft is 16.5 feet wide'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm Orion width as 16.5 feet (16 1/2).

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule offers about 330 cubic feet of habitable space for the four crew members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Orion capsule only has about 330 cubic feet of habitable space' for four crew. R5: 'habitable volume of around 330 cubic feet' for crew.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state ~330 cu ft habitable volume in Orion for the crew.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket has a liftoff weight of 2,600 tonnes (5.76 million lbs).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'When fully fuelled, the rocket weighs 2,600 tonnes (5.76 million lbs)'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly matches the exact liftoff weight figures for the SLS rocket.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket is shorter than the 363-foot Apollo-era Saturn V.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '322 feet tall is shorter than the 363-feet tall Saturn V'
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly compares SLS height (322 ft) as shorter than Saturn V (363 ft).

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket is more powerful than the Apollo-era Saturn V.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'shorter than the 363-feet tall Saturn V ... but about 17% more powerful'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states SLS is more powerful than Saturn V.
